aspects.says: ConcurrentHashMap, the skip-list collections, the concurrent queues and ArrayDeque refuse null, so that null from get or poll means absent or empty without a second call; the copy-on-write classes accept it.
basis: section:ConcurrentHashMap Refuses null, So That null from get Means Absent

aspects.says: A CopyOnWriteArrayList iterator works over the array as it was when iteration began: it never throws ConcurrentModificationException, and changes made during the loop show from the next iteration.
basis: section:CopyOnWriteArrayList Copies Its Array on Every Write, So Readers Iterate a Snapshot

aspects.says: Every write to a CopyOnWriteArrayList copies the whole array, which suits a listener list written a few times and read on every event.
basis: section:CopyOnWriteArrayList Copies Its Array on Every Write, So Readers Iterate a Snapshot
aspects.reason: a cost claim no deterministic test can observe; unit 6.5.2 measures it

aspects.says: Taking from the front of an ArrayList shifts every remaining element; an ArrayDeque takes from either end at a cost that does not grow with its size.
basis: section:A Collection Costs What Its Structure Makes It Cost: ArrayList by Index, ArrayDeque at the Ends
aspects.reason: a cost no deterministic test can observe without timing; the page shows the measurement

aspects.says: A HashSet or HashMap iterates in the order of its hash table, which is not insertion order and changes when the table resizes; LinkedHashSet and LinkedHashMap keep first-insertion order.
basis: section:A Hash Set Iterates in Hash Order, and the Order Changes as the Set Grows

aspects.says: get(i) on a LinkedList walks from the nearer end, so a loop by index over it is quadratic, while an ArrayList reaches any index directly.
basis: section:A Collection Costs What Its Structure Makes It Cost: ArrayList by Index, ArrayDeque at the Ends

aspects.says: The two-argument subSet and headSet include the lower bound and exclude the upper one; the four-argument forms set each bound.
basis: section:A Sorted Set Answers Ranges Through Views Backed by the Set

aspects.says: subSet, headSet and tailSet return views that follow later changes to the set; a result that must stay fixed is a copy.
basis: section:A Sorted Set Answers Ranges Through Views Backed by the Set

aspects.says: A stand-in for null in a map that refuses null must be a value no caller can store; an empty string collides with a real empty value.
basis: section:ConcurrentHashMap Refuses null, So That null from get Means Absent
